(p-261) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Saba'

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the Hereafter﴾. We have already mentioned, at the beginning of Surah al-Fatihah, in the discussion of His saying ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah: 2], what has the same meaning from the verses.

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 34, verse 2:

﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving.﴾ In this noble verse, He, may His majesty be exalted, makes clear that He ﴿knows what enters into the earth﴾, i.e., what enters it, such as the water descending from the sky that enters into the earth, as He clarified with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth?﴾ [az-Zumar: 21], and the verse continues.

And His saying: ﴿And We send down water from the sky in a measured amount, and We settle it in the earth﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18], so He, may His majesty be exalted, knows the number of the drops descending from the sky to the earth. And how would He not know it, when He created it: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-Mulk: 14]. He also knows what enters into the earth of the dead who are buried in it, as He, may His majesty be exalted, said: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55], and He said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ ﴿for the living and the dead?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 25–26]. Al-kifat (ٱلْكِفَاتُ), from the root kafata, means gathering and drawing together, because the earth gathers them while living upon its surface and, when dead, within its belly. He also knows what enters into the earth of seeds, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Not a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. Likewise, He knows what is in its belly of minerals and other things.

His saying: ﴿and what comes out of it﴾, i.e., out of the earth, such as plants and grains, minerals, treasures, hidden stores and other things. And He knows ﴿what descends from the sky﴾ of rain, snow, hail, provision, and other things. And ﴿what ascends into it﴾, i.e., ascends into it, meaning into the sky, such as the good deeds (p-262) ﴿righteous deeds﴾, as He explained with His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10], and such as the souls of the believers and other things, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4], and the verse continues.

And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He arranges the affair from the sky to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a Day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count﴾ [as-Sajdah: 5]. What He, may His majesty be exalted, mentioned in this noble verse, that He knows all that was mentioned, He mentioned in Surah "al-Hadid" in His saying: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving. And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us."﴾ [al-Hadid: 4].

We have clarified the verses indicating the perfection of Allah's comprehensive knowledge of everything at the beginning of Surah "Hud," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their breasts to hide from Him﴾ [Hud: 5], and in many other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾ In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that the disbelievers denied the resurrection and said, ﴿The Hour will not come to us﴾, meaning the Resurrection. He, majestic and exalted, commanded His Prophet to swear to them by his great Lord that the Hour would surely come upon them, emphasizing this with multiple emphases.

What He, majestic and exalted, mentions in this noble verse concerning the disbelievers' denial of resurrection is clarified in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾ [an-Nahl: 38],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, will I really be brought forth alive?"﴾ [Maryam: 66],

• and His saying about them: ﴿And we will not be resurrected﴾ [al-An'am: 29], ﴿And we will not be raised up﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 36] [sic: 66],

and verses of this kind are very numerous. What He, majestic and exalted, mentions, that He commanded His Prophet to swear to them that they will be resurrected, is clarified in other places.

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir of this noble verse: "This is one of the three verses, which have no fourth, in which Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to swear by his great Lord to the occurrence of the Return, since those among the people of disbelief and obstinacy denied it. The first of them is in the surah of Yunus, peace be upon him, and it is His saying, exalted is He: (p-263) ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true, and you cannot escape."﴾ [Yunus: 53]. The second is this: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾ The third is in the surah of at-Taghabun, and it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did"﴾ up to the end of the verse [at-Taghabun: 7]."

We have already presented the proofs indicating resurrection after death from the Qur'an in surat al-Baqarah, surat an-Nahl and others.

We have also presented the verses indicating the disbelievers' denial of resurrection and what Allah has prepared for those who deny resurrection of punishment in al-Furqan, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing fire﴾ [al-Furqan: 11], and in other places. As for His saying "Say, 'Yes'" (qul bala), the word bala: we have already presented its meanings in the Arabic language with clarification in surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they will submit, "We did not used to do any evil." Yes﴾ up to the end of the verse [an-Nahl: 28].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Knower of the unseen; not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth, nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear record.﴾ What He, majestic and exalted, mentions in this noble verse, that not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater, is clarified in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you are not in any matter, and do not recite from it any Qur'an, and you do not do any deed except that We are witnesses over you when you are involved in it. And not absent from your Lord is an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear record﴾ [Yunus: 61], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and the sea. And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but that it is in a clear record﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. The verses of this kind are numerous, and we have explained them in several places of this blessed book.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: "la yaʿzub" means: is not absent from Him, an atom's weight. From it is the saying of Ka'b ibn Sa'd al-Ghanawi:

My brother, as for his forbearance, it is abundant upon him, and as for his ignorance, it is absent (ʿazīb).

(p-264) He means: ignorance is absent from him; he is not characterized by it. This letter was read by Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir: ʿĀlimu al-ghayb, with an alif after the ʿayn, lightening of the lam, and the mim pronounced with a dammah, on the pattern of fā'il. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: ʿAllāmi al-ghayb, with a shaddah on the lam, an alif after the doubled lam, and the mim with a kasrah, on the pattern of fa''āl. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and 'Asim read: ʿĀlimi al-ghayb, like the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir, except that they pronounce the mim with a kasrah. On the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir with the dammah on the mim, in "ʿĀlimu al-ghayb," it is a subject whose predicate is the clause "la yaʿzubu ʿanhu" (the verse), or the predicate of an elided subject, meaning: He is the Knower of the unseen.

On the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and 'Asim: ʿĀlimi al-ghayb, with the kasrah on the mim, it is an adjective of "rabbī" (my Lord), meaning: say, "Yes, by my Lord, Knower of the unseen, you will surely be..." and likewise on the reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i: ʿAllāmi al-ghayb. The majority of readers other than al-Kisa'i read this letter: la yaʿzubu ʿanhu, with a dammah on the zay of yaʿzubu, and al-Kisa'i read it with a kasrah on the zay.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 5:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, for them is a painful punishment of wretchedness﴾. Here He did not specify the type of this punishment, but He specified it in His saying in "al-Hajj" (the pilgrimage): ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Hajj: 51]. His saying "mu'ajizin" (seeking to frustrate them) means contending and competing, supposing that they can outdo their Lord, so that He is not able to resurrect them and punish them. "Rijz" (wretchedness) means punishment, as He said: ﴿So We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from heaven﴾ and so on [al-Baqarah: 59]. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited this word as "mu'ajjizin" (without an alif after the ʿayn, with the jim kasra shaddah), while the rest recited it with an alif after the ʿayn and a light jim. The meaning of the shaddah reading is that they suppose they can outdo their Lord, so that He is not able to resurrect them and punish them.

Some scholars said: the meaning of "mu'ajjizin" with the shaddah is "mu-tabbitin" (discouraging), that is, discouraging people from faith. Ibn Kathir and Hafs recited "min rijzin alimun" with a damma on the mim of "alimun," considering it an adjective (na't) of "adhab" (punishment), while the rest recited "alimin" with a kasra, considering it an adjective of "rijzin."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you are completely disintegrated, you will be [re]created in a new creation?"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...in extreme error.﴾ (p-265) What this noble verse contains of the denial of resurrection (al-ba'th) and God's refutation of them in that matter has been set forth in many places in this book, in al-Baqarah, an-Nahl, and elsewhere.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿when you are completely disintegrated﴾, meaning: your bodies are torn apart and scattered, your bones decay, mix with the earth, and vanish into it. His saying about them: ﴿indeed you are in a new creation﴾, meaning: resurrection after death, which is the target of their denial (may God disfigure them), while He, exalted and high, knows what has dissolved into the earth of their bodies and bones, as He said, may He be exalted: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record﴾ [Qaf: 4].

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 9:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them, of the heaven and the earth?﴾ What this noble verse indicates is the rebuke and reproach of the disbelievers for their failure to reflect and to look at what is before them and behind them, of the heaven and the earth, so that they might thereby deduce the perfection of Allah's power over the resurrection, and over everything, and that He alone is the one worthy of worship. This is made clear in other places,

such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it and adorned it, and it has no cracks? And the earth, We spread it out and cast into it firmly set mountains and caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind, as an insight and a reminder for every servant turning back in repentance﴾ [Qaf: 6-8],

and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and at what things Allah has created, and that perhaps their term has drawn near?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185],

and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And how many a sign there is in the heavens and the earth that they pass by, while they turn away from it!﴾ [Yusuf: 105].

Verses of this kind are many and well known.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his commentary on this verse: Abd ibn Humayd said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them, of the heaven and the earth?﴾ [Saba': 9]. He said: If you look to your right, or to your left, or in front of you, or behind you, you will see the heaven and the earth.

* *

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or We shall drop upon them fragments from the sky.﴾ In this noble verse Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions two matters:

The first: that if He wills, He will cause the earth to swallow the disbelievers; He will make it swallow them, by virtue of His power to do so.

The second: that if He wills to drop upon them fragments from the sky, He will also do that, by virtue of His power over it.

As for the first, namely that if He willed to cause the earth to swallow them, He would do so: He has mentioned this in other places,

such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Are you secure from the One in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16],

and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Are you then secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you?﴾ – the verse [al-Isra': 68],

and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us﴾ [al-Qasas: 82],

and His saying, Exalted is He, in "al-An'am": ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾ – the verse [al-An'am: 65].

As for His saying here: ﴿or We shall drop upon them fragments from the sky﴾, we have already explained in the surah of "Bani Isra'il" that this is what is meant by His saying, Exalted is He, concerning the disbelievers: ﴿or You cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed﴾ – the verse [al-Isra': 92].

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿If He wills, He will cause the earth to swallow them, or He will drop upon them fragments from the sky﴾ with the letter ya' (third person) in the three verbs, namely yasha' (يَشَأْ), yakhsif (يَخْسِفْ) and yuskit (يُسْقِطْ). According to this reading, the subject is a pronoun referring back to Allah, Exalted is He, meaning: if He, that is Allah, wills, He will cause the earth to swallow them. The rest of the readers recited with the letter nun, which indicates majesty, in the three verbs, meaning: if We will (nasha'), etc. Hafs, on the authority of Asim, recited kisafan (كِسَفًا) with a fatha on the sin, while the rest recited it with a sukun on it. Al-kasaf (الكَسَفُ) with a fatha on the sin means pieces, and al-kisf (الكِسْفُ) with a sukun on the sin is its singular.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 10:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentioned that He gave David a bounty from Himself, which He bestowed upon him. He explained this bounty that He bestowed upon David in other verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And David killed Goliath, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him from what He willed﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 251],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive speech﴾ [Sad: 20],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave to David Solomon; how excellent a servant he was; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah]﴾ [Sad: 30],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾ [Sad: 25],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth﴾ [Sad: 26],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly given David and Solomon knowledge; and they said, "All praise is due to Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants"﴾ [An-Naml: 15],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have favored some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Zabur﴾ [Al-Isra': 55],

and other verses besides these.

(p-267) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mountains, repeat [the praises] with him, and the birds﴾.

We have already clarified the verses that explain this, together with clarifying the meaning of ﴿repeat [the praises] with him﴾ in Surah "Al-Anbiya'", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Us] with David, and the birds, and We were doing [that]﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 79].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ ﴿saying, "Make full coats of armor and calculate well the links [of chain armor]"﴾.

We have already presented the verses in which this is explained, along with some evidence, and the explanation of His saying: ﴿and calculate well the links﴾, in Surah "Al-Anbiya'", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We taught him the making of armor for you﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 80]. And in "An-Nahl", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And garments that protect you from your violence﴾ [An-Nahl: 81].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind; its morning [journey was] a month's [travel], and its evening [journey was] a month's [travel].﴾

We have already explained the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Anbiya'" (The Prophets), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing swiftly by his command toward the land﴾ [al-Anbiya': 81], up to the end of the verse, together with the answers to some of the questions raised concerning the aforementioned verses.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord﴾, up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and large basins like reservoirs and cooking pots fixed firmly [in their places]﴾. We have already presented the verses that elucidate this in Surah "al-Anbiya'", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among the devils were those who dived for him and performed other work than that; and We were their guardians﴾ [al-Anbiya': 82].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 17:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-372) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Saba'

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do We requite [anyone] except the ungrateful?﴾

This noble verse, according to both recitations, the recitation with a damma on the yā' and a fatḥa on the zāy, in the passive voice, with "al-kafūr" in the nominative as the deputy of the subject (nā'ib al-fā'il), and the recitation of "nujāzī" with a damma on the nūn and a kasra on the zāy, in the active voice, with "al-kafūr" in the accusative as the direct object (maf'ūl bihi), indicates the specificity of the recompense to those who go to excess in disbelief.

Other verses have come indicating the generality of the recompense, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7], and so on.

The answer to this is in three respects:

The first: the meaning is that We do not requite this severe, uprooting recompense except the one who goes to great lengths in ingratitude.

The second: what is done to other than the disbeliever by way of recompense is not punishment in reality, because it is purification and expiation (tamhis).

The third: that no one is requited for all deeds with complete scrutiny (munaqashah tammah) except the disbeliever. This is indicated by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever has his account scrutinized, he will perish." And when 'Ā'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, asked him about His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he will be judged with an easy account and will return to his family joyful﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 8-9], he told her that this was the intent, and explained to her that whoever has his account scrutinized is bound to perish.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Iblis certainly found his assumption about them to be true, so they followed him, except for a party of the believers﴾. I have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He, quoting him: ﴿I will surely make evil seem attractive to them on the earth, and I will surely mislead them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 39]. And in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful﴾ [al-A'raf: 17], and His saying: ﴿Certainly [sadaqa]﴾. It was read by 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i with the doubled dal (saddaqa), while the rest read it with the single dal (sadaqa).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter﴾ – the verse.

We have already explained the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ – the verse [al-Hijr: 40], and in other places besides that.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth﴾ — the verse. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him, and they will not have the power to remove the harm from you or to change it﴾ [al-Isra' 17:56].

Allah's statement: ﴿And intercession will not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Al-Baqarah," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿Nor will intercession be accepted from it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 48].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 24:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to say to the disbelievers: ﴿Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ That is: who provides for you from the heavens, by sending down rain for example, and from the earth, by causing crops and fruits to grow, and the like. Then He commanded him to say: "Allah." That is: the One who provides for you from the heavens and the earth is Allah. His, the Exalted's, command to him (ﷺ) to answer that their provider is Allah implies that they acknowledge this, and that it is not a matter of dispute.

Allah, the Exalted, has stated this explicitly in many verses, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living?﴾ Their acknowledgment of His lordship obliges them to recognize that worship is due to Him alone, and to know this.

We have already presented many verses clarifying this in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ [al-Isra: 9].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 25:

(p-269) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: You will not be questioned about what we committed, nor will we be questioned about what you do.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to say to the disbelievers: indeed, they and he are such that none of them is answerable for what the other does; rather, each of them is held accountable for his own deed, and the other is free of it.

He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, then say: For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do.﴾ [Yunus: 41]; and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾ [al-Kafirun: 1-6]. And with a similar meaning in general is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is a nation that has passed away; for them is what they earned, and for you is what you have earned, and you will not be questioned about what they used to do.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 141]; and like His saying about His Prophet Hud, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet: ﴿He said: Indeed I call Allah to witness, and bear witness that I am free of what you associate besides Him. So scheme against me all together, then do not give me respite.﴾ [Hud: 54-55].

The Almighty said to His Prophet ﷺ in this noble verse: ﴿Say: Show me those whom you have joined with Him as partners. Nay! Rather, He is Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ Allah, Mighty and Exalted, commanded His Prophet ﷺ in this noble verse to say to the idol-worshippers: "Show me your idols which you have joined with Allah as partners in His worship, [a sign of] your disbelief, your polytheism and your fabrication." His saying ﴿Show me those whom you have joined with Him as partners﴾ is because, if they showed Him these idols, it would become clear upon seeing them that they are inanimate objects that neither benefit nor harm, and their remoteness from the attributes of divinity would become evident. Thus it would become manifest to every intelligent person, by seeing them, that worshipping what neither benefits nor harms is false. Bringing them forth and discussing them, while they are present to be seen, is more eloquent than discussing them while they are absent, although he ﷺ knew them. Just as in this noble verse He commanded them to show Him these idols so that the falsehood of worshipping them would become evident, so in another verse He commanded them to name them, because naming them by their names reveals their remoteness from the attributes of divinity and the falsehood of worshipping them, since they are names of lowly females, such as al-Lat, al-Uzza and Manat, the third, the other. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but females﴾ [An-Nisa: 117] and related to this His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or have they assigned to Allah partners? Say: Name them. Or will you inform Him of what He knows not on earth, or [is it] mere outward speech? Rather, the plan of those who disbelieved has been made attractive to them, and they have been averted from the way. And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 33].

The more apparent meaning of His saying ﴿Show me those whom you have joined with Him﴾ in this verse is what we have mentioned: that the seeing is visual (basariyyah), and according to this, His saying "shurakaa'" (partners) is a hal (circumstantial accusative). Some scholars said that it is from ra'a in the sense of knowing ('ilmiyyah), and according to this, "shurakaa'" is the third object (maf'ul thalith) of "arunee" (show me). Al-Qurtubi said: "Here arunee may be from the seeing of the heart, so shurakaa' is a third object, meaning: inform me of the idols and images which you have made partners of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and whether they shared in the creation of anything. So state what they are, otherwise why do you worship them?" (end of quotation), the relevant point of which is noted. Abu Hayyan also chose this in "al-Bahr al-Muhit." His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: "Nay!" is a rebuke for them and a deterrence from associating partners with Him. His saying: ﴿Nay! Rather, He is Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ means: the one characterised by that is the one deserving of worship. We have already mentioned the meaning of "al-Aziz al-Hakim" with its evidences many times.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. We have already presented the verses clarifying this in surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and in other places. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿except comprehensively to mankind﴾, some scholars of Arabic grammar (ʿulamaʾ al-ʿArabiyyah) cited it as evidence for the permissibility of a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, ḥāl) preceding its possessor (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) when that possessor is governed by a preposition (ḥarf), as Ibn Malik indicated in his "al-Khulasa" with his saying:

And the preceding of a ḥāl when its possessor is governed by a particle of genitive, they have refused it, but I do not prohibit it, for it has come.

They said: because the meaning is ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾, i.e., all of them, meaning: We have sent you to mankind while they are gathered in your message. Among those who permitted this were Abu ʿAli al-Farisi, Ibn Kaysan, and Ibn Burhan, and there are witnesses for it in the poetry of the Arabs, such as the saying of Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi:

? If camels have been seized and women, they will not go away empty-handed for the killing of Ḥibāl.

And the saying of Kuthayyir:

? Though the coolness of water is thirsty-stricken, longing toward me, beloved, indeed it is beloved.

And the saying of another:

? I have consoled myself, all of you, after your separation, by remembering you, until it is as if you were with me.

And the saying of another:

? Heedless, death confronts the man, so he is called, and there is no time for refusal.

(p-271) And his saying:

? Passionately devoted to you, you have been passionately loved, but only the parting has been decreed, and there is no way to you.

And his saying:

? When a man's manliness has defeated him in youth, its pursuit becomes difficult for him in maturity.

So his saying in the first verse, "fargan" (empty), means "in vain," is a ḥāl, and its possessor is the genitive governed by the preposition "bi" which is in "bi-qatl," and "Ḥibāl" is the name of a man. His saying in the second verse, "hayman, ṣādiyan," are two ḥāls from the first-person pronoun suffix governed by "ila" in his saying "ilayya ḥabīban." His saying in the third verse, "ṭurran," is a ḥāl from the pronoun governed by "ʿan" in his saying "ʿankum." Thus, the preceding of the ḥāl over its possessor governed by a particle was rejected by the majority of the grammarians.

Al-Zamakhshari said in "al-Kashshaf," in explaining His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾: "except as a general message encompassing them, for when it encompasses them, it has sufficed them so that none of them can go out of it."

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: We have sent you gathering mankind in warning and conveying, and he made it a ḥāl from the kaf (of "arsalnaka"). According to this, the taʾ (in "kaffa") should be for emphasis (mubalagha), like the taʾ in "rawiyah" and "ʿallamah." Whoever makes it a ḥāl from the genitive, preceding it, has erred, because the preceding of the ḥāl of a genitive upon it is, in terms of impermissibility, like the preceding of the genitive upon the particle. How many are those who commit this error and are not content with it until they add to it that the lam is taken to mean "ila," for the first error cannot be made correct except by the second error, so they must commit both errors. End of his words.

Al-Shaykh al-Sabban said in his gloss on al-Ashmuni: al-Zamakhshari made "kaffah" an adjective of a deleted verbal noun, i.e., "a message comprehensive for mankind," but it has been objected that "kaffah" is specific to rational beings and is in the accusative as a ḥāl, like "ṭurran" and "qāṭibah." End of the relevant point from him. What al-Sabban mentioned about "kaffah" is the well-known and commonly used usage in Arabic speech, and Abu Hayyan clarified this in "al-Bahr." And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: For you is the appointment of a Day from which you cannot delay by an hour nor advance [it]﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Yunus," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For every nation is a term; when their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance [it]﴾ [Yunus: 49].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿when you used to command us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him﴾. We have mentioned some of the verses that clarify this in Surah al-Baqarah, in discussing His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿when those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166], and we have explained it in other places in this Blessed Book.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved﴾. This has been clarified in other places:

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains﴾ [Ghafir: 71],

• and His saying: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles around their necks﴾ [al-Ra'd: 5],

• and His saying: ﴿Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, insert him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 32],

and other verses besides these.

Allah's statement: ﴿Never did We send a warner to a town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with."﴾ We have already explained the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-An'am," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And thus We placed in every town its greatest criminals﴾ [al-An'am: 123], and we made this clear in Surah "Qad aflaha al-mu'minun," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 44] and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "We are greater in wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children that will bring you near to Us in position.﴾ We have already presented the verses clarifying this in surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination.﴾ [al-Kahf: 36]

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 36:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾. [p. 272] We have already explained the verses that clarify this in Surah al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray﴾ [al-An'am: 116], and in other places besides it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all together, then He will say to the angels, "Did these worship you?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn"﴾ — the verse.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Furqan," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them and what they worshipped besides Allah, and He will say, "Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You; it was not for us to take any protectors besides You, but You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the reminder"﴾ — the verse [al-Furqan: 17–18].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is none but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship."﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:94].

Allah's statement: ﴿And We did not give them any scriptures which they could study, nor did We send to them before you any warner.﴾ We have already presented the verses that have this same meaning in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach a tenth of what We had given them, so they denied My messengers. Then how was My rejection?﴾ What Allah, exalted and majestic is He, mentions in this noble verse is that He destroyed the earlier nations when they denied His messengers, and that the earlier nations were stronger, and had more wealth and children, and that the disbelievers of Makkah should fear the destruction of Allah upon them because of their denial of His Messenger ﷺ, just as He destroyed the nations that were stronger than them. "They were not given" means the disbelievers of Makkah were not given a tenth (mi'shar) of what Allah gave the nations He destroyed before them of strength. This is clarified in many verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They were more numerous than them and mightier in strength and in traces left upon the earth﴾ [Ghafir: 82]. We have already presented some discussion of this in Surah "al-Rum," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they tilled the earth and cultivated it more than they cultivated it﴾ [al-Rum: 9].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then reflect: there is no madness in your companion. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Mu'minun," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"? Rather, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 70].

Al-Shinqiti's commentary (*Adwa' al-Bayan*) on Surah 34, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is for yourselves﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth for it. My reward is only from Allah﴾ [Hud: 29].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Dispelling the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is for yourselves. My reward is only from Allah﴾, the verse.

This noble verse indicates that he (ﷺ) did not ask his community for any reward for conveying to them what came to them of good in this world and the Hereafter. Similar to it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not of those who impose [what is not theirs]﴾ [Sad: 86], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ [al-Tur: 40] in Surah al-Tur, and [in Surah] al-Qalam [al-Qalam: 46]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord﴾ [al-Furqan: 57], and His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it. It is only a reminder to the worlds﴾ [al-An'am: 90].

Not asking a wage for conveying the message is the practice of all the messengers, upon them be the blessings and peace of Allah, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Follow the messengers. Follow those who do not ask you for any reward﴾ [Ya-Sin: 20–21]. And He, may He be exalted, said in Surah al-Shu'ara': ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109], in the story of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb, upon them and upon our Prophet be prayer and peace.

He said in Surah Hud, concerning Nuh: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth for it. My reward is only from Allah, and I will not drive away those who have believed﴾, the verse [Hud: 29].

He also said in it concerning Hud: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it. My reward is only from the One who created me﴾, the verse [Hud: 51]. But there has come in another verse what gives the appearance of the opposite of that, namely His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, except affection among the near of kin﴾ [al-Shura: 23].

Know first that in His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿except affection among the near of kin﴾ there are four opinions:

The first: It was narrated by al-Sha'bi and others from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and others also said it, as Ibn Jarir and others transmitted from them, that the meaning of the verse, ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, except affection among the near of kin﴾, is: except that you love me for my kinship that is between me and you, so that you restrain your harm from me and protect me from the harm of people, just as you protect everyone who has a kinship with you similar to my kinship with you.

He (ﷺ) had a blood relationship in every clan of Quraysh. So what he asked of them was not a reward for conveying the message, because it is granted to everyone, since everyone's kin love him and defend him against the harm of people. Abu Talib did this for him, yet it was not a reward for conveying the message, because he did not believe. And if he did not ask any reward except this thing which is not a reward, it is established that he did not ask any reward, like the saying of al-Nabigha:

*"There is no fault in them, except that their swords are notched by the clashing of the battalions."*

(p-٣٧٤) Such a usage the rhetoricians call *ta'kid al-madh bima yushbihu al-dhamm* (affirming praise in a form resembling dispraise), and this opinion is the correct one regarding the verse. Ibn Jarir chose it, and according to it there is no difficulty.

The second: The meaning of the verse, ﴿except affection among the near of kin﴾, is: do not harm my relatives and my family, and protect me regarding them. This opinion is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and according to it there is also no difficulty, because affection among the Muslims is obligatory among them, and the closest of kin to the Prophet (ﷺ) [have the greatest claim to it]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71].

And in the hadith: "The likeness of the believers in their mercy, their love and their affection is like one body: when one of its limbs is afflicted, the rest of the body responds to it with sleeplessness and fever." And he (ﷺ) said: "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself." The hadiths on this are very numerous. And if the religion itself requires this among the Muslims, it becomes clear that it is not a compensation for conveying the message.

Some scholars said: The exception is *munqati'* (disconnected) according to both opinions, and according to it there is no difficulty.

So its meaning according to the first opinion is: I do not ask you for any reward for it, but I remind you of my kinship among you.

And according to the second: But I remind you of Allah regarding my kinship, so protect me concerning them.

The third opinion, and this is what al-Hasan said: ﴿except affection among the near of kin﴾, that is, except that you draw close to Allah and seek nearness to Him through obedience and righteous deeds. According to it there is also no difficulty, because drawing near to Allah is not a reward for conveying the message.

The fourth opinion: ﴿except affection among the near of kin﴾, that is, except that you show affection to your relatives and maintain your ties of kinship. Ibn Jarir mentioned this opinion from 'Abd Allah ibn Qasim.

According to it too there is no difficulty, because a person's maintaining of the ties of kinship is not a reward for conveying the message. You have come to know the correct interpretation of the verse, and the resolution of the difficulty has become clear to you according to all the opinions.

As for the claim that His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿except affection among the near of kin﴾ is abrogated (*mansukh*) by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is for yourselves﴾ [Saba': 47], this is weak. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor restore.﴾

I have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And say: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish.﴾ [Al-Isra': 81].

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 34, verse 50:

"He said, the Exalted: ﴿Say, 'If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment, and if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me.'﴾"

We have already presented the verses that carry this same meaning in Surat al-Anbiya', in the discussion of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78], in the context of explaining the proofs of the Zahiriyya (the literalist school) for their claim that ijtihad (independent legal reasoning) is prohibited.

He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "We believe in it." But how can they reach it from a distant place?﴾

What this noble verse includes, namely that the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection will believe in Allah, and that this belief will not benefit them because the time of its benefit has passed, which is the period of the life of this world, has been clarified in many verses.

We have already presented the verses that indicate this in Surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth"﴾ [al-A'raf: 53]. And in Surah "Maryam," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿How [clearly] will they hear and see the Day they come to Us! But the wrongdoers today are in clear error﴾ [Maryam: 38], and in other places. His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And how can they reach it from a distant place?﴾, "anna" (how/whence) here indicates complete astonishment at the improbability. "Al-tanawush" (التناوش) means "al-tanawul" (reaching, taking hold of). Some scholars said it is specifically the easy reaching of a thing that is near.

The meaning is: it is considered utterly improbable, and it is extremely far, that the disbelievers should reach the beneficial faith in the Hereafter after they wasted it at the time when it was possible, in the abode of this world. It was also said that the astonishment is at their being returned to the world once more so that they could believe. The first is more apparent, and his saying before it supports it: ﴿They said, "We believe in it."﴾ Whoever wishes to reach something from a distant place cannot do so. And Allah knows best.
